ai.title: Virtualize agent store list
ai.summary: Agent store page now virtualizes the 'All Agents' grid using @tanstack/react-virtual. New useResponsiveColumns hook adjusts column count (1-3) based on viewport width, splitting agents into rows for the virtualizer. Virtualization activates only when rows exceed 6, reducing DOM load on large lists.

eli5.text: The agent store page on the web now loads faster when there are many agents listed. Instead of rendering every agent's full card in the browser at once, it only shows the ones visible on your screen and swaps in new rows as you scroll through the 'All Agents' grid. The page also adjusts how many agent cards appear side by side depending on your screen width, fitting one card across on a phone, two on a tablet, and three on a desktop, with virtualization kicking in only when the list gets long enough to need it. This change is already live today.

ai.title: Refactor referral client and add back button fallback
ai.summary: Referral page logic moved from server component to new `referral-client.tsx`, replacing `referral-client-wrapper.tsx`. `BackButton` now accepts optional `fallbackUrl` prop, used in agent detail page to navigate to `/store`. This consolidates client-side referral code storage and improves navigation reliability.

eli5.text: When someone clicks a referral link to join Codebuff, the page now stores their referral code more reliably in the browser before showing the signup screen, so the credit is less likely to get lost. The back button on an agent's detail page now has a safety net: if there's no history to go back to, it sends you to the store page instead of doing nothing. You would notice a smoother experience landing on a referral page and a back button that actually takes you somewhere useful even on a fresh visit.

ai.title: CustomToolDefinition Args/Input generics constrained to Record
ai.summary: Type parameters Args and Input in CustomToolDefinition and getCustomToolDefinition now extend Record<string, unknown>. This replaces the previous unknown constraint, enforcing object-shaped arguments and inputs at the type level. Affects sdk/src/custom-tool.ts only.

eli5.text: When defining a custom tool, the assistant now requires arguments and inputs to be object-shaped rather than any arbitrary value, so you can build tools that rely on a predictable, dictionary-style structure instead of guessing at loose inputs. This only affects how tools are typed at design time; existing tools keep working and you would only notice it if you were constructing the type signature yourself.

ai.title: Revert @agent prefill, pass --agent directly
ai.summary: Removed logic prefilling `@agent` into `initialInput`. `--agent` flag now passed directly to `codebuff` as `agent` parameter. Affects `npm-app/src/index.ts`.

eli5.text: If you ask me to run with a specific helper by name, I now hand that name straight to the engine instead of typing it in for you first. This only matters when you start me up with that helper flag set, and nothing else changes about how a normal session begins. The old trick of me typing "@helper" into the first line is gone, so if you looked, you'd just see the helper name passed through directly rather than showing up as your opening message. It's live now.

ai.title: Skip agent DB validation errors in development
ai.summary: validateSpawnableAgents now suppresses invalid agent ID errors when NODE_ENV is 'development'. This prevents noisy database warnings during local agent config development. Affects shared core validation logic in common/src/util/agent-template-validation.ts.

eli5.text: When you're building or changing an agent's setup on your own computer, the system will now stay quiet if it can't find that agent in the database, instead of showing a warning. If you tried to use an agent ID that isn't saved yet, nothing would pop up telling you it's missing while you're still working locally. This only happens during development, so if you publish or run it elsewhere, the check comes back on.

ai.title: Web UI responsive fixes and login flow update
ai.summary: Implemented responsive layout adjustments across web app pages including agent metrics, publisher profiles, and store views. Updated login card to support session-based navigation with referral and CLI auth code handling. Changes affect `web/src/app/publishers`, `web/src/app/store`, and `web/src/components/login` files.

eli5.text: When you open the app on a phone or smaller screen, pages like your profile, the store, and agent usage charts now spread out or stack neatly instead of getting cramped or cut off. The sign-in screen was also updated so that after you log in you can return straight to the page you were heading to, and links from email or the command-line tool work as intended. You'd notice cleaner layouts with less sideways scrolling and a smoother transition from signing in to getting back to your work.

ai.title: Update .env.example NEXTPUBLICCBENVIRONMENT to dev
ai.summary: Changed default NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT from development to dev in .env.example. Aligns example configuration with expected environment variable values. Affects local setup and documentation accuracy.

eli5.text: When someone sets up the software on their own computer for the first time, they copy a sample settings file and fill in the blanks. That sample file used the word 'development' for the environment setting, but the software actually expects the word 'dev'. Changing it so the sample matches what the software looks for means the setup instructions now lead to a working local environment without that small mismatch tripping up new developers.

Changes affect repo docs and environment templates only.

eli5.text: Two minor documentation updates were made today for people contributing to the project: the setup guide now includes steps for giving yourself free service credits in a local test account, and a settings file was corrected to point to the proper analytics website address. These changes only affect written instructions and example templates, so nothing in the actual software behaves differently today; if you looked, you would just see updated text in a guide and a fixed web address in a setup file.

ai.title: CONTRIBUTING.md formatting tweak
ai.summary: CONTRIBUTING.md restructures 'Running in other directories' section. Nested list items replace sequential a./b. steps. Code blocks indented under bullets. Pure documentation formatting.

eli5.text: The instructions for contributors on how to run the software from different folders got a small cleanup: the old a./b. numbered steps were turned into bulleted lists, and the example commands are now indented under each bullet so they line up better. If you look at the file you'll see the words stayed the same, but the layout is tidier, making it easier to follow which command belongs to which step. This is only documentation formatting, so nothing about how the software works actually changed.
